summary.headline: VST Tillers FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR1,240 crore; Q4 revenue up 9% to INR328 crore, operational EBITDA margin 14.2%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 25% year on year to about INR1,240 crore (transcript also cites INR1,248 crore), led by power tillers, which grew 35% to 50,332 units. Q4 revenue rose 9% to INR328 crore, with operational EBITDA margin of 14.2% versus 13.4% a year earlier, and operational PAT (excluding fair value gains/losses) up 36% to about INR39 crore. Management declined to guide FY27 growth, citing fuel and commodity inflation, a monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA, and fertiliser availability concerns; it said April and May demand was good and expects Q1 growth over the prior year. Price hikes were taken across tillers and tractors at the end of April.

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 50,332 units incl. exports, up 35% from 37,297; Q4 volume 12,958 vs 13,278 a year earlier (down year on year). Management called it the highest-ever annual volume.

segments.name: Domestic tractors
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic volume 4,596 units, up 18.6%; Q4 domestic volume 1,244 units, up about 20%. Q4 tractor exports rose to 430 units from 260.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 11,346 units vs 7,458 (about 52% growth); Q4 volume 2,947 units, up 27%. Front and rear rotary weeders launched in Q4.

segments.name: Power reapers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 3,464 units, up 44%; seasonal, so minimal Q4 volume.

segments.name: Zetor / higher-HP tractors
segments.commentary: Single 8+2 variant (3.5 litre engine) currently; FY26 target is about 1,000 units; target 5,000-6,000 units by FY30. Sold through a few dealerships with month-on-month volume increases.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number; aspiration is 25% growth, with Q1 FY27 expected to grow over the prior year and Q2 dependent on how events unfold.
Operational EBITDA margin expected in a 12% to 14% range, versus the earlier 11% to 13% guidance.
Earlier stated path of 23% to 26% CAGR through FY30 toward INR3,000 crore revenue was reiterated as the goal, but management said current realities make this uncertain.
Zetor 4WD variant and additional variants planned this year; Netherlands-based European operation to launch in June/July 2026.
US market re-entry (electric tractor drivetrains): trials from 2026, product launch by end-2027.
All-India launch of electric weeders and electric tillers planned for early Q2 FY27.
Retail finance penetration to rise from about 10% in FY26 to a target of 20% in FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Project Chatrapati: village-level workers appointed and many new retail counters opened to extend small and marginal farmer reach.
Supply chain: TOC-based model; SRM module being rolled out to give suppliers visibility of GRN and payments.
demand_pricing: April 2026 grew in both tractors and tillers; May demand described as good so far.
Price increases taken across power tillers and tractors towards end of April 2026; management said only part of the inflation had been passed through so far.
Cost pressure from fuel and commodity price rises; operational efficiencies are buffering margins for now.
Industry commentary: management agreed high base and flat agri income mean high growth is unlikely to continue; exact FY27 industry outcome hard to predict.
Fertiliser availability described as a likely problem, with no specific data; monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 and the FY30 growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; it is tracking month by month and quarter by quarter, expects Q1 growth over the prior year, and targets 25% but said specifics are difficult to call given uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins be maintained with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to a 12% to 14% operational EBITDA margin range, up from 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for the Zetor brand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 1,000 Zetor units in FY27 and 5,000 to 6,000 by FY30, with more variants and a 4WD variant to come.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and the European business shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 export momentum was better; Netherlands-based operation to launch in June/July 2026 as planned, and management is confident of export growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory held at about 36 days; receivables cut from about 75 days to 51 days, with further reduction targeted over the next 2 to 3 years via the TOC supply chain model and SRM digitisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large investment balance be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Three areas: technology and products, global expansion (US re-entry with launch by end-2027), and inorganic opportunities in adjacencies; no specific deal announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the electric tractor investment in Zimeno Inc (US)?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment already provisioned for; US subsidy removal and tariffs halted drivetrain exports. Expertise gained is being used to launch electric weeders and tillers first, with an all-India launch planned for early Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Fuel and commodity inflation may not be fully passed on to customers if it persists.
Monsoon distribution and timing (IMD forecast 92% of LPA) could affect farm incomes and machinery demand.
Fair value losses on investments continue to affect reported PAT; Q4 loss was heavier than in Q3.
Q4 tillers volume declined year on year (12,958 vs 13,278); watch whether this recurs.
Zetor volumes depend on a limited dealer footprint and are at an early stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and margins, but notably cautious and evasive on FY27 growth, repeatedly declining to quantify it and citing monsoon, inflation and fuel-price uncertainty.
key_quotes: We are at a strong 14.2% of operational EBITDA against 13.4%, which is roughly 80 basis points of improvement.
We have sold highest number of power tillers in the year, which is more than 50,000 number, reflecting a very strong growth of 35%.
We are positive that we will be able to operate between 12% to 14%.
